tagline: 30,000 islands, 7 million ferry trips a year, and a public operator already ordering electric ferries. The archipelago commute is begging to be foiled.
summary: Stockholm is built on water — a capital spread across islands at the mouth of a 30,000-island archipelago, where boats are not tourism but daily life. The public operator Waxholmsbolaget runs 35+ routes carrying roughly 7 million passengers a year, and the city and operator have begun ordering electric ferries as Sweden pushes maritime decarbonisation. Long, scenic, protected-water commuter legs out to Vaxholm, Sandhamn, Grinda and the outer skerries are exactly the kind of corridors where foiling's combination of speed, smoothness and zero emissions compounds — turning a 1-2 hour displacement-ferry slog into a fast, clean commute, while the summer archipelago-tourism surge adds a premium leisure layer.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The whole core archipelago network — Vaxholm (~13 nm), Sandhamn (~30 nm), Nynäshamn (~28 nm), Grinda and inner-city routes — sits comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on flat, sheltered Baltic archipelago water, with both commuter volume and a decarbonising public operator.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reaches the far outer skerries and longer Baltic legs (e.g. toward Gotland staging) beyond the all-electric range without depending on charging at small island piers.

competitive_landscape: Waxholmsbolaget and SL dominate with a large displacement fleet now beginning to electrify. Incumbent battery ferries will be clean but slow; foiling competes by being faster AND zero-emission, compressing long archipelago commutes in a way battery-converted displacement hulls cannot.
seasonality: Commuting is year-round (with winter ice in the inner archipelago a constraint on the outermost legs); leisure demand surges intensely in the Jun-Aug Swedish summer. The electrification push is season-independent, anchoring a durable market.
regulatory_note: Region Stockholm, SL and Waxholmsbolaget are actively procuring electric ferries as part of Sweden's transport-decarbonisation agenda; clean propulsion is increasingly a procurement requirement, favouring zero-emission foiling entrants.
